body:
FLiBe at Li₂BeF₄ stoichiometry (2:1 LiF:BeF₂ molar ratio) enriched to ≥90% ⁶Li delivers the highest tritium breeding ratio chemically achievable, with tritium extracted via continuous inert-gas sparging exploiting T₂ and HT volatility from the melt.

*Why:* ⁶Li(n,α)T is the sole productive breeding reaction; maximising ⁶Li atom density in the blanket volume therefore maximises TBR. The 2:1 LiF:BeF₂ eutectic (melting point ~459 °C) provides the highest Li molar fraction a BeF₂-stabilised melt can sustain before viscosity and BeF₂ polymerisation become operationally prohibitive. Be moderates fast neutrons into the thermal range where ⁶Li cross-section peaks (~940 b at thermal), amplifying the effective reaction rate beyond what pure LiF would achieve with 14 MeV source neutrons alone. Tritium partitions as T₂/HT into the cover gas at ppb-level solubility in the melt, allowing helium sparging to strip it continuously without chemical reprocessing of the bulk salt.

*Testable:*
- TBR for 2:1 LiF:BeF₂ at ≥90% ⁶Li enrichment exceeds 1.05 in a tokamak blanket geometry with a 60 cm FLiBe zone, while dropping below 1.0 if ⁶Li enrichment falls below 30%.
- Increasing BeF₂ fraction beyond the 2:1 ratio (e.g. to 1:1 LiF:BeF₂) decreases TBR despite added Be moderation, because Li atom density falls faster than the thermal-flux gain compensates.
- Tritium partial pressure over 2:1 FLiBe at 500–650 °C is sufficient (>10⁻⁴ Pa per wppm dissolved T) that a helium sparge flow of <1 L/min per MW of fusion power maintains dissolved T below 1 wppm.
- The 2:1 melt remains single-phase and pumpable (viscosity <20 mPa·s) up to at least 700 °C, while compositions with >40 mol% BeF₂ gel above the eutectic and cannot be circulated.

*Shaky:*
- Be neutron multiplication via ⁹Be(n,2n) is already counted in most TBR estimates but the Q-value and angular distribution are sensitive to the fast-flux spectrum; if the blanket sees a softer spectrum than assumed, the multiplication gain shrinks and TBR may fall short of 1.05.
- Tritium permeation through structural steel at 600 °C is non-trivial; the sparge extraction efficiency depends on tritium not preferentially migrating to the wall before reaching the cover gas, which is unverified at high Be loading.
- ⁶Li enrichment above 90% is expensive and introduces isotopic cascade complexity; cost pressure may force operation at 60–70% enrichment, which our TBR prediction says crosses below the viability threshold.

*Confidence* 0.72

The claim that 2:1 LiF:BeF₂ maximises TBR against richer BeF₂ mixtures neglects the ⁹Be(n,2n) neutron multiplier, whose contribution is not marginal. In a 14 MeV-driven DT blanket the fast flux above the 2.7 MeV ⁹Be(n,2n) threshold is substantial before thermalisation. Published OpenMC/MCNP blanket sweeps (e.g. Sauvan et al. 2018 Nucl. Fusion, Abdou ITER blanket studies) consistently show TBR peaking at BeF₂ mole fractions of roughly 35–40 mol% — i.e. closer to 1.5:1 LiF:BeF₂, not 2:1 — precisely because the (n,2n) multiplication gain from the additional Be more than offsets the modest Li density reduction in that window. The 2:1 stoichiometry sits at ~33 mol% BeF₂; shifting toward ~40 mol% BeF₂ increases the total neutron population feeding ⁶Li capture before the Li penalty dominates. If that peak is at ~1.5:1 rather than 2:1, the proposal's optimal composition is wrong even if its physical reasoning is directionally correct, and the second testable prediction — that TBR monotonically falls as you add BeF₂ beyond 2:1 — is also wrong in the 33–40 mol% window. The hypothesis needs a neutronics sweep to establish where the actual TBR maximum sits, which is exactly what the proposal currently asserts rather than derives.

*On:* The second testable prediction: "Increasing BeF₂ fraction beyond the 2:1 ratio (e.g. to 1:1 LiF:BeF₂) decreases TBR despite added Be moderation, because Li atom density falls faster than the thermal-flux gain compensates."

FLiBe at approximately 38–40 mol% BeF₂ (roughly 1.5:1 LiF:BeF₂) enriched to ≥90% ⁶Li maximises TBR among chemically viable FLiBe compositions, with tritium extracted via continuous helium sparging.

*Why:* ⁶Li(n,α)T is the only productive breeding reaction, so TBR is the product of the ⁶Li atom density and the effective neutron population available to it. At 33 mol% BeF₂ (2:1 eutectic), ⁹Be(n,2n) multiplication is already operating, but the fast flux above the 2.7 MeV threshold supports additional multiplication as BeF₂ rises toward ~40 mol%. In the 33–40 mol% window the neutron multiplication gain from incremental Be outpaces the fractional loss in Li atom density, shifting the TBR maximum away from the 2:1 eutectic. Above ~40 mol% the Li penalty dominates and TBR falls. Tritium extraction mechanism is unchanged: T₂/HT partitions into the cover gas at ppb-level solubility, stripped by helium sparging.

*Testable:*
- A BeF₂ composition sweep at 90% ⁶Li enrichment shows TBR peaking between 36–42 mol% BeF₂, with the 33.3 mol% eutectic sitting measurably below (by ≥0.02 TBR units) the optimum.
- TBR at 40 mol% BeF₂ / 90% ⁶Li exceeds 1.10 in a 60 cm blanket zone, while TBR at 33.3 mol% BeF₂ / 90% ⁶Li is between 1.05–1.10 — both above unity, but the 40 mol% point is higher.
- Increasing BeF₂ beyond 42 mol% at any fixed ⁶Li enrichment ≥90% causes TBR to decline, confirming the peak is interior to the 33–46 mol% range.
- The 38–40 mol% composition remains single-phase and pumpable (viscosity <30 mPa·s) at 500–650 °C — physically operable, if somewhat more viscous than the 2:1 eutectic.

*Shaky:*
- The precomputed interpolation dataset backing the commissioned sweep may not resolve the 33–40 mol% window finely enough to distinguish a shallow peak from a plateau — the TBR difference may be within interpolation error.
- At 38–40 mol% BeF₂, melt viscosity rises and single-phase stability narrows; if the composition drifts under irradiation or partial freeze, operability degrades without a compensating TBR gain.
- If the blanket neutron spectrum is softer than the DT-forward assumption (e.g. due to thicker first-wall steel), the fast-flux available for ⁹Be(n,2n) shrinks and the peak may shift back toward lower BeF₂, restoring the 2:1 eutectic as practical optimum.

*Confidence* 0.65

The revised optimum at 38–40 mol% BeF₂ is chemically inviable as a circulating coolant at the proposed operating temperatures. The FLiBe liquidus rises steeply with BeF₂ content: the 2:1 eutectic (33.3 mol% BeF₂) melts at ~459 °C, but the liquidus at 40 mol% BeF₂ climbs to roughly 530–560 °C (Cantor 1968 ORNL-TM-2316; Williams et al. 2006 ORNL/TM-2006/12). More critically, viscosity in this composition range is not a gentle increase — BeF₂-rich melts undergo network polymerisation of BeF₄²⁻ tetrahedra that causes viscosity to jump non-linearly: measured values at 38–40 mol% BeF₂ near the liquidus exceed 100 mPa·s, not 30. The proposal's "<30 mPa·s" figure is taken from the 2:1 eutectic at 600 °C and cannot be extended to the revised composition without evidence. A blanket coolant that freezes at ~550 °C and gels during any transient cool-down cannot be safely circulated, which means the proposed optimal composition fails the chemical viability criterion that was the original constraint of the hypothesis. The TBR gain — even granting the ~0.02 unit improvement — is irrelevant if the fluid cannot be pumped through the blanket.

*On:* The fourth testable prediction: "The 38–40 mol% composition remains single-phase and pumpable (viscosity <30 mPa·s) at 500–650 °C — physically operable, if somewhat more viscous than the 2:1 eutectic."

FLiBe at the 2:1 LiF:BeF₂ eutectic stoichiometry (33.3 mol% BeF₂, melting point ~459 °C), enriched to ≥90% ⁶Li, is the chemically viable composition that maximises tritium breeding ratio, with tritium recovered by continuous helium sparging.

*Why:* ⁶Li(n,α)T is the sole productive breeding reaction, so TBR is set by the product of ⁶Li atom density and the effective neutron population reaching it. Be moderates fast neutrons below 2.7 MeV where the ⁶Li cross-section peaks (~940 b thermal) and also provides ⁹Be(n,2n) multiplication above 2.7 MeV. Although the neutronics optimum sits near 36–40 mol% BeF₂, the liquidus at those compositions rises to 530–560 °C and viscosity exceeds 100 mPa·s near the liquidus due to BeF₄²⁻ network polymerisation — rendering those melts unacceptable as circulating blanket coolants. The 2:1 eutectic is the highest-BeF₂ composition that clears both the thermal-hydraulic floor (liquidus ~459 °C, viscosity ~6 mPa·s at 600 °C) and the operability margin against freeze transients. Its TBR, while ~0.02 units short of the unconstrained neutronics peak, remains above unity with ≥90% ⁶Li enrichment. Tritium partitions as T₂/HT into the cover gas at ppb-level melt solubility, stripped efficiently by helium sparging without bulk reprocessing.

*Testable:*
- TBR for 2:1 FLiBe at 90% ⁶Li enrichment in a 60 cm blanket zone exceeds 1.05, while any composition with >42 mol% BeF₂ at identical enrichment yields lower TBR despite the additional Be, because the Li-density penalty dominates above that threshold.
- A BeF₂ composition sweep from 33–45 mol% shows a shallow TBR maximum near 36–40 mol%, but compositions in that window have liquidus temperatures ≥530 °C and viscosities ≥50 mPa·s near operating temperature, disqualifying them on chemical-operability grounds.
- Helium sparging at <1 L/min per MW fusion power maintains dissolved tritium in 2:1 FLiBe below 1 wppm at 500–650 °C, given tritium partial pressure >10⁻⁴ Pa per wppm dissolved T.
- TBR drops below 1.0 at ⁶Li enrichments below 30% for the 2:1 composition in a standard 60 cm blanket geometry, establishing enrichment ≥90% as operationally necessary rather than merely optimal.

*Shaky:*
- The TBR advantage of the 2:1 eutectic over the 38–40 mol% window is only ~0.02 units; if the blanket geometry or spectrum differs from the standard DT tokamak assumption, the practical ranking could reverse even within the operable composition range.
- Tritium permeation through structural steel at 600 °C may remove a significant fraction before helium sparging captures it, particularly if permeation rate at the 2:1 composition exceeds the stripping rate — this is unverified at scale.
- ⁶Li enrichment ≥90% adds isotopic cascade cost and supply-chain risk; commercial deployment pressure at 60–70% enrichment would push TBR below the 1.05 target, and the operability advantage of 2:1 over richer BeF₂ would then need to be re-examined against a lower-enrichment 36–38 mol% alternative.

*Confidence* 0.74

## Verdict

**1. FLiBe at the 2:1 LiF:BeF₂ eutectic stoichiometry (33.3 mol% BeF₂, melting point ~459 °C), enriched to ≥90% ⁶Li, is the chemically viable composition that maximises tritium breeding ratio among circulating-blanket-compatible FLiBe melts, with tritium recovered by continuous helium sparging.**

⁶Li(n,α)T is the sole productive breeding reaction; TBR is the product of ⁶Li atom density and effective neutron population. Be moderates fast neutrons into the thermal range where the ⁶Li cross-section peaks (~940 b) and provides ⁹Be(n,2n) multiplication above 2.7 MeV. The neutronics-only optimum sits near 36–40 mol% BeF₂, but BeF₄²⁻ network polymerisation at those compositions raises the liquidus to 530–560 °C and viscosity to ≥100 mPa·s near the liquidus, disqualifying them as circulating coolants. The 2:1 eutectic is the richest-BeF₂ composition that remains single-phase and pumpable (liquidus ~459 °C, viscosity ~6 mPa·s at 600 °C) with an adequate freeze-transient margin. Tritium partitions as T₂/HT into the cover gas at ppb-level melt solubility and is stripped continuously by helium sparging without bulk salt reprocessing.

*Standing.* This is the surviving hypothesis after four rounds, but it survives by constraint elimination rather than positive confirmation. The Proposer originally claimed 2:1 as the neutronics optimum; the Reviewer correctly refuted that, citing published sweeps showing TBR peaking near 38–40 mol% BeF₂. The Proposer conceded the neutronics point entirely and shifted to a chemical-operability argument: the unconstrained neutronics peak is inaccessible because those compositions freeze and gel under operating conditions. The Reviewer's second objection — citing ORNL liquidus data (Cantor 1968, Williams 2006) and the non-linear viscosity jump from BeF₄²⁻ polymerisation — directly attacked the revised 38–40 mol% hypothesis and succeeded; the Proposer accepted the physical chemistry and retreated to 2:1. The final hypothesis thus rests on two accepted facts: (1) the neutronics peak is near 36–40 mol% BeF₂, and (2) those compositions are thermally and rheologically inoperable. Neither fact was contested in the final round. What was never established by argument or simulation is whether the 2:1 composition itself meets TBR >1.05 at ≥90% ⁶Li in the specific blanket geometry under discussion — the numbers are taken from prior literature without a geometry-specific neutronics run. The helium-sparging extraction mechanism was proposed in round 1 and never challenged; it stands as uncontested but also unvalidated.
*Confidence.* 0.62

*Predictions.*
- TBR for 2:1 FLiBe at 90% ⁶Li enrichment in a 60 cm blanket zone exceeds 1.05; compositions above 42 mol% BeF₂ at identical enrichment yield lower TBR because the Li-density penalty dominates.
- A BeF₂ sweep from 33–45 mol% shows a shallow TBR maximum near 36–40 mol%, but those compositions have liquidus ≥530 °C and viscosity ≥50 mPa·s near operating temperature, disqualifying them on operability grounds.
- Helium sparging at <1 L/min per MW fusion power maintains dissolved tritium below 1 wppm at 500–650 °C, given tritium partial pressure >10⁻⁴ Pa per wppm dissolved T over 2:1 FLiBe.
- TBR drops below 1.0 at ⁶Li enrichments below 30% for the 2:1 composition in a 60 cm standard blanket geometry.

**2. FLiBe at approximately 38–40 mol% BeF₂ (roughly 1.5:1 LiF:BeF₂) enriched to ≥90% ⁶Li maximises TBR among FLiBe compositions without operability constraints applied.**

In the 33–40 mol% BeF₂ window, ⁹Be(n,2n) neutron multiplication above the 2.7 MeV threshold adds to the total neutron population feeding ⁶Li capture faster than the fractional loss of Li atom density. Above ~40 mol% the Li-density penalty dominates and TBR declines. The peak is interior to the operable composition range only in a neutronics sense.

*Standing.* This hypothesis was proposed by the Reviewer in round 2 as a direct refutation of the original 2:1 optimum claim, and the Proposer accepted it in round 3. However, the Reviewer then refuted it on operability grounds in round 4, citing ORNL thermophysical data the Proposer did not contest. The hypothesis survives as a neutronics statement — that the unconstrained TBR maximum is near 38–40 mol% BeF₂ — but fails as a practical recommendation because the composition cannot be safely circulated. No simulation was commissioned to confirm the neutronics claim, so even the neutronics standing is literature-supported but not independently verified in the debate. It ranks below the eutectic hypothesis solely because the debate applied an operability constraint that the topic explicitly required ('chemically viable to extract from blanket').
*Confidence.* 0.45

*Predictions.*
- A BeF₂ composition sweep at 90% ⁶Li shows TBR peaking between 36–42 mol% BeF₂, with the 33.3 mol% eutectic measurably below (≥0.02 TBR units) the peak.
- TBR at 40 mol% BeF₂ / 90% ⁶Li exceeds 1.10 in a 60 cm blanket zone, versus 1.05–1.10 at 33.3 mol% BeF₂.

**Why this order.** The debate moved through three distinct positions: (1) 2:1 eutectic as neutronics optimum (refuted by the Reviewer on neutron-multiplication grounds); (2) 38–40 mol% BeF₂ as neutronics optimum (accepted by the Proposer, then refuted by the Reviewer on thermophysical-operability grounds); (3) 2:1 eutectic as the best chemically viable composition (accepted by both parties in the final round). The final consensus is narrow: both sides agree the unconstrained neutronics peak is near 38–40 mol% BeF₂, and both agree those compositions are thermally and rheologically inoperable under blanket conditions, leaving the 2:1 eutectic as the best viable option. Confidence is set below the Proposer's 0.74 because the specific TBR values (>1.05, enrichment threshold) were never confirmed by a commissioned simulation and rest on literature interpolation for a generic blanket geometry, not the one under discussion. The helium-sparging extraction method was uncontested throughout but also unvalidated at scale.

**Unresolved.**
- The TBR of the 2:1 LiF:BeF₂ eutectic at ≥90% ⁶Li in the specific tokamak blanket geometry under consideration was never computed in this debate. A salt-neutronics-tbr sweep from 30–45 mol% BeF₂ at fixed 90% ⁶Li enrichment in that geometry would confirm whether TBR >1.05 is achievable at the eutectic and precisely where the peak sits.
- The ~0.02-unit TBR advantage of the 38–40 mol% composition over the 2:1 eutectic was asserted from prior published sweeps; it may be within numerical or interpolation error. The same neutronics sweep would resolve whether the peak-to-eutectic TBR difference is real and large enough to motivate engineering workarounds for the operability problem.
- Whether any thermal-management or composition-control strategy (e.g., operating at higher bulk temperature, adding a small LiF excess, or accepting a narrower freeze margin) could make the 36–38 mol% range circulate-able while preserving most of the TBR gain is unexplored. A salt-chemistry-md simulation at 36–40 mol% BeF₂ near the liquidus would bound the viscosity and phase-stability question more precisely than the 1968 ORNL data allow.
- Tritium permeation through structural steel at 600 °C relative to helium-sparge stripping rate is unresolved. This determines whether dissolved tritium actually stays below 1 wppm or whether wall permeation is the dominant loss channel, undermining the extraction viability claim. No experimental or simulation pathway was identified to close this gap in the debate.
- The impact of reduced ⁶Li enrichment (60–70% vs. ≥90%) on TBR at the 2:1 eutectic, and whether a slightly richer-BeF₂ melt at lower enrichment could compensate, was raised as a concern but left entirely unanalysed. This is the commercially critical operating regime and deserves a dedicated neutronics sweep.
